learner_level: medical students, ophthalmology residents and early specialty trainees
description: A broad, subspecialty-spanning ophthalmology curriculum map covering foundational sciences, clinical assessment, medical and surgical subspecialties, emergencies, rehabilitation and professional practice. It is a structured starting blueprint: local faculty must map it to the applicable national and institutional curriculum, training stage and examination blueprint.

coverage_expectations: Foundational ocular anatomy, embryology, physiology, optics and visual neuroscience
Clinical history, examination, diagnostic techniques and investigation interpretation
Cornea, ocular surface, external disease, lens, cataract and refractive surgery
Glaucoma, uveitis, medical retina, retinal vascular disease and vitreoretinal surgery
Neuro-ophthalmology, ocular motility, pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus
Oculoplastics, orbit, lacrimal disease, ocular oncology and pathology
Trauma, emergency ophthalmology, ocular infection and systemic disease
Pharmacology, anaesthesia, perioperative care, microsurgery, lasers and procedures
Low-vision rehabilitation, community ophthalmology, evidence-based practice and ethics

safeguards: Never treat search rank, popularity, deck downloads or challenge scores as evidence quality
Never let an exam-prep page or community Anki deck independently establish clinical recommendations
Preserve provenance and link to the original source
Do not bypass paywalls, logins, robots rules, rate limits or terms of service
Do not store or redistribute full third-party content unless reuse rights explicitly allow it
If a source is unavailable or its licence is unclear, retain a link and mark it link_only or rights_unknown
All clinical claims and generated answers remain pending qualified faculty review

source_coverage_policy.target: At least two independent resource types should be discoverable for each topic where feasible; absence is a visible coverage gap, not a reason to invent sources.
source_coverage_policy.required_distinction: Separate learning resources, exam-practice resources and clinical evidence; do not collapse them into one undifferentiated source score.
source_coverage_policy.freshness: Store publication/update and retrieval dates; flag time-sensitive clinical material for review.
source_coverage_policy.conflict_handling: Conflicting recommendations create a faculty-review item with jurisdiction and date context; do not auto-resolve clinical disagreement.

source_selection_rules: Prefer current professional-society guidelines for clinical management; record jurisdiction, version and update date.
Use PubMed searches to select individual systematic reviews, trials and observational studies relevant to the exact learning objective.
Use open-access full text only after checking the article-level reuse licence; repository availability alone is not permission to reproduce.
Use Anki, DoctorDE and public exam-preparation material only as exam-practice signals, never as independent clinical evidence.
Map each selected item to explicit objective IDs and record why it is relevant.
Keep all source records unreviewed until a qualified ophthalmology faculty reviewer verifies relevance, currency, methodology, conflicts and local applicability.
Only add an excerpt to reference_sources after confirming it is permitted to store; an excerpt must be a short, source-faithful quotation or faculty-authored paraphrase explicitly labelled as such.

strict_generation_gate.reason: Discovery links and bibliographic metadata do not count as evidence excerpts in usiphus_evidence.py.
